sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 of the 1925 East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch below the key map and index. It shows Market Street running across the sheet from the western edge, where a note points 750 feet west to St. Leo's rectory on a detached inset, eastward past Brookside Avenue to the borough's eastern blocks. Brookside Avenue runs south from Market Street at the lower left, with a short row of small dwellings and a pair of greenhouses on its east side and a row of numbered lots (28 to 57) fronting Market Street. The middle of the part is taken by the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad and its sidings, which cross Market Street diagonally; a curving branch track runs south-west from the crossing. North of Market Street along the tracks lie the J. & J. List Lumber Co. yard with long lumber sheds and lumber piles, the Bergen County Cut Stone Co., and George F. Bracket's contractor yard with machinery and asphalt sheds. The rest of the part is large open lots (115, 120, 121, 124) with scattered dwellings and outbuildings. The top-left inset (St. Leo's R.C. Church, school and rectory on Market Street) is a separate part and is not covered here; the key map at the top of the sheet is not georeferenced.
notes: J. & J. List Lumber Co., Bergen County Cut Stone Co. and George F. Bracket contractor yard lie along the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad north of Market Street.
The railroad crossing Market Street here is abandoned today (OpenStreetMap former NYS&W line).

Placed from Brookside Avenue / Market Street and a point derived along Market Street at the atlas scale; the railroad crossing in today's data lies about 28 m from where the sheet draws it, so the placement is low confidence.

Scale 100 ft (lower half); key map at 1000 ft and index, water and fire department notes in the upper half (not georeferenced). Two parts: part 1 the lower map of Market Street at Brookside Avenue with the NYS&W Railroad, J. & J. List Lumber Co., Bergen County Cut Stone Co. and G. F. Bracket contractor yard; part 2 a framed inset at the top left of the lower half showing St. Leo's R.C. Church, school and rectory on Market Street, 750 ft west of Brookside Avenue (not placed). North points about 12 degrees left of up. Part 1 placed by a hand-picked Brookside Avenue / Market Street point plus a derived point along Market Street (low confidence).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: St. Leo's R.C. Church, school and rectory on Market Street (no street junction; only Market Street drawn, placed 750 ft west of Brookside Avenue by a note; needs step 6b: a point on Market Street located from the 750 ft note or from St. Leo's church site, plus a derived point along Market Street).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is the one sheet of the atlas drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers the Dundee Lake industrial area at the south-western edge of the borough, between River Drive at the top and the Passaic River and River Road at the lower left, with Market Street crossing the lower right corner. Grove Street meets River Drive at the top edge. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad (Erie line) crosses the sheet diagonally on a 100 ft right-of-way, bridging the river at the lower left. West of the tracks, beside a pond, stand the Crews Piece Dye Works: dye house, finishing building, machine shop, engine room, water purifiers and an asbestos-protected store house. East of the tracks the National Silk Dyeing Co. Dundee Lake Works fills most of the sheet: dye houses, finishing and folding buildings, preparing and drying, receiving and office building, singe building, color mixing and storage, printing, engraving, gray wash room and roll storage, with sections marked being built, a fire-proof brick store house, machine shop, pipe shop, oxidizing building, garage, reservoir, service tanks, a precipitating pit and two 180,000 gallon fuel oil tanks. A second pond lies south of the works. Notes on the sheet say the surveyor was not admitted to the National works and that the diagram was taken from F.I.A. maps. A few dwellings on lots 610 to 613 face Market Street at the lower right.
notes: National Silk Dyeing Co., Dundee Lake Works: admittance refused; diagram and information taken from F.I.A. maps, buildings marked being built drawn in the field.
Crews Piece Dye Works: surveyor admitted to the grounds but not to the buildings.
Drawn at 50 ft to an inch, unlike the rest of the atlas (100 ft).
Placed by two hand-picked points only (Grove Street / River Drive and the railroad crossing of River Road), so the placement is low confidence.

Scale 50 ft (the only 50 ft sheet). Dundee Lake works: National Silk Dyeing Co. (Dundee Lake Works) and Crews Piece Dye Works, ponds, NYS&W (Erie line) railroad, River Drive and Grove Street at the top, River Road and the Passaic River at the lower left, Market Street at the lower right. Turned like the other sheets (north about 71 degrees left of up). No detectable junction: placed by hand-picked Grove Street / River Drive and the railroad crossing of River Road (low confidence).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the western residential grid of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) between Gilbert Avenue and Summit Avenue, and between Grant Street and Speidel Avenue at the top and River Drive and a pond at the bottom. The long north-south streets Gilbert, Falmouth, Philip and Miller Avenues and Lee, Orchard and Grove Streets are crossed by Speidel Avenue, Summit Street and Elm Street; Grant Street and North Street appear at the upper right and West, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets are named at the right margin. Most blocks are platted in narrow numbered lots, many still vacant, with frame dwellings, a few stores and greenhouses scattered through them. Buildings of note are the Gilbert Avenue School standing alone in a large open tract (44) west of Gilbert Avenue, the Fire Department (Defender Co. No. 1) on Grove Street, and the Corin Chemical Works with a raised building and storage on River Drive near Philip Avenue. The pond at the lower right belongs to the Dundee Lake works on sheet 2. A heavily framed inset at the lower left (River Drive and Orchard Street at River Road) is a separate part and is not covered here.
notes: Summit Street is today Viviney Street.
Gilbert Avenue School, Corin Chemical Works and Fire Department Defender Co. No. 1 are drawn on this part.

Scale 100 ft. Main part: Gilbert Avenue to Summit Avenue, Grant and Speidel to River Drive; Summit Street is today Viviney Street. Part 2 is a framed inset at the lower left (River Drive, River Road, Orchard Street, Pantana Silk Co. broad silk mill, ice house) with its own north arrow; not placed. Sheet turned about 71 degrees (north to the left).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: River Drive and Orchard Street at River Road (Pantana Silk Co., ice house) (the drawn arrangement (Orchard meeting River Road, River Drive at the top) does not match any modern junction with confidence; needs identification of River Road / River Drive as drawn against today's River Drive, then step 6b).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the north-central part of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) between Gilbert Avenue and North Street, from East 54th Street at the top to Oak Avenue and the blocks beyond it at the bottom. Gilbert, Falmouth, Philip and Miller Avenues and Lee and Orchard Streets run up the sheet, joined in the upper half by Walnut, Beech and Pine Streets and Main Avenue; Spruce, Maple, Cedar and Oak cross them, and Gall Street and Center Street are named at the right margin. The lower and middle blocks are subdivided into numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings; the upper blocks between East 54th Street and Spruce are larger tracts with several greenhouses on concrete bases. The East Fifty-fourth Street School stands on Main Avenue near East 54th Street, an auto repair shop opposite, and another greenhouse lies on Orchard Street near North Street. A large open tract (44) fills the western margin beyond Gilbert Avenue. A dash-dot match line at the bottom right marks the edge of sheet 5.
notes: Oak Avenue is today Mola Boulevard.
Walnut Street is today part of Philip Avenue, Beech Street part of Miller Avenue and Pine Street part of Lee Street.
Maple and Cedar no longer exist as streets.
East Fifty-fourth Street School on Main Avenue.

Scale 100 ft. Gilbert Avenue to North Street, East 54th Street to Oak; Oak is today Mola Boulevard, Walnut part of Philip Avenue, Beech part of Miller Avenue, Pine part of Lee Street. East 54th Street School. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the southern centre of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) from North and Summit Avenue on the west to Locust Street and Market Street on the east, and from Grant Street at the top to River Drive at the bottom. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally with Railroad Avenue beside it; the Tide Water Oil Co. oil tanks and pump stand at the top by South Street, the Jaffe Coal Co. coal pocket and sheds and the Dundee Lake passenger station lie along the tracks further south. West of the railroad are large lots on Grant and West Streets and small blocks on 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets off Summit Avenue. East of it a fan of narrow lots lies between Chamberlain Avenue, Paterson Avenue, South Center, Muller and Garfield Streets, then Coates, Church, Oak and Chestnut Streets around Van Riper Avenue. The East Paterson Presbyterian Church, a hotel, auto repair shops, a garage and a blacksmith shop stand near Church Street and Market Street, the post office and the Market Street School on Market Street, and greenhouses in the open tract (122) east of Locust Street. Lot numbers continue onto the neighbouring sheets.
notes: South Center Street is today Center Street and South Center Street; South Street is today Linden Avenue.
Muller and Garfield Streets and Railroad Avenue are gone; the Christopher Columbus Highway runs through the area today.
Tide Water Oil Co., Jaffe Coal Co., Dundee Lake passenger station, East Paterson Presbyterian Church, post office and Market Street School.

Scale 100 ft. North Street and Summit Avenue to Locust Street and Market Street, Grant Street to River Drive; NYS&W railroad with Railroad Avenue, Tide Water Oil Co., Jaffe Coal Co., Presbyterian church, Market Street School. South Center is today Center / South Center Street; Muller, Garfield, Railroad Avenue gone. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern edge of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) between North Street and the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad, from Lopez Street (marked arbitrary) at the top to Center Street at the bottom. East 54th Street runs diagonally from the left margin down to Van Riper Avenue, which curves south toward the railroad. Franklin Street and John Street run between East 54th Street and the blocks below; Gall Street crosses the sheet below them, with South Street and Sudek Lane running down to Center Street. In the upper right, beyond Van Riper Avenue, are small blocks on Lincoln and Wallice Streets. Most of the area is large undivided tracts (82, 83, 90, 91, 101, 115, 116) with scattered dwellings, sheds and greenhouses; a small cemetery lies on Lopez Street. Development is thicker along East 54th Street, Gall Street and South Street.
notes: South Street is today Linden Avenue, Center Street is today Mola Boulevard, Gall Street is Gall Avenue.
Sudek Lane continues the line of Franklin Street south of Gall Street; today's Franklin Street follows it.
Lopez Street is marked arbitrary (a name given by the surveyor); Lincoln and Wallice Streets do not survive.
Scale 100 ft. North Street to the NYS&W railroad, Lopez (arbitrary) to Center Street; South is today Linden Avenue, Center is Mola Boulevard. Mostly large open tracts. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the northern part of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park), the Columbia-Magnolia grid between Willow Street and Broadway, from Cyril Avenue at the top to River Drive and the Passaic River at the bottom. Florence Place, Elizabeth, Bellevue, Rosedale, Orange, Rosemont and Parkview Avenues cross Willow, Columbia and Magnolia Streets and Broadway. The blocks are platted in small numbered lots with frame dwellings spread thinly across them; a few tile and brick houses and the Fire Department (Defender Co. No. 2) on Parkview Avenue stand out. The right-of-way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) cuts diagonally across the south-western blocks. The Saddle River Township line runs along the top and down the western margin, where a column of lots fronts the township side. East of Broadway are the golf links with the Elmwood Country Club club house and locker room; Sterling Street leaves Broadway at the bottom right. The Passaic River with the City of Paterson beyond fills the bottom of the sheet. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Cyril Avenue and Florence Place.
notes: Magnolia Street is lettered Magonila on the sheet.
Parkview Avenue is today Park View Avenue.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right-of-way, Elmwood Country Club and Fire Department Defender Co. No. 2.
Orange Avenue junctions with Willow and Magnolia Streets disagree with today's street lines by about 10 m and were left out.

Scale 100 ft. Willow Street to Broadway, Cyril Avenue to River Drive and the Passaic River; North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. right-of-way, golf links and Elmwood Country Club. Magnolia lettered Magonila. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 8 covers the north-eastern blocks of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) between Broadway at the top and 16th Avenue, and between East 53rd Street and East 55th Street, with a strip of blocks west of East 53rd Street on 15th and 16th Avenues. 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th Avenues cross East 53rd, East 54th and East 55th Streets; the blocks are cut into narrow numbered lots, many still vacant, with frame dwellings, a few stores near Broadway and a greenhouse on concrete base at East 53rd Street. The First Presbyterian Church stands on 16th Avenue between East 53rd and East 54th Streets. East of East 55th Street run the Erie Railroad (Bergen County branch) and the borough line, with Saddle River Township beyond and a short arbitrary street, Delphine, at the right edge. The part is drawn with north toward the top, unlike most sheets of the atlas, which are turned about 70 degrees.
notes: First Presbyterian Church on 16th Avenue.
Delphine Street is marked arbitrary on the index.

Scale 100 ft (entire sheet), drawn with north up (rotation about +19 degrees, unlike the other sheets). Three parts: part 1 Broadway to 16th Avenue between East 53rd and East 55th Streets; part 2 Martha and Kipp Avenues from River Drive to Beech Street; part 3 Martha and Kipp Avenues from block 131 (Bank Street) to Cole Street. Parts 2 and 3 lie along the Garfield borough line.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 8 is a strip along the southern borough line with Garfield, showing Martha Avenue and Kipp Avenue from River Drive and the Passaic River in the west to Beech Street in the east, with Ann Street crossing between them. The blocks (122, 131, 132, 133, 134) are platted in narrow numbered lots, mostly vacant, with a few frame dwellings, a shed and a store near River Drive. The borough line runs along the bottom of the strip, below which the sheet says to see the map of Garfield; a large brick building at the right edge below Kipp Avenue belongs to Garfield. It continues eastward in part 3 of the same sheet, drawn below it on the page.
notes: Beech Street here no longer exists under that name; only the Ann Street, River Drive junctions were used for control (4 points).

Scale 100 ft (entire sheet), drawn with north up (rotation about +19 degrees, unlike the other sheets). Three parts: part 1 Broadway to 16th Avenue between East 53rd and East 55th Streets; part 2 Martha and Kipp Avenues from River Drive to Beech Street; part 3 Martha and Kipp Avenues from block 131 (Bank Street) to Cole Street. Parts 2 and 3 lie along the Garfield borough line.

sheet-8-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 8 continues the southern strip of East Paterson (now Elmwood Park) east of part 2, along Martha Avenue and Kipp Avenue from block 131 to Cole Street, crossed by Bank, Ray, Page and Mill Streets. The blocks (122, 123, 127 to 131, 135, 136) are cut into narrow numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings and sheds; a row of lots north of Martha Avenue and a small block (123) beside Cole Street complete the strip. The borough line with Garfield runs along the bottom edge and the sheet refers to the map of Garfield there; the N.Y.S. and W. railroad switch appears at the lower right corner. A north arrow and the sheet's scale bar are drawn in this part.
notes: Scale 100 ft (entire sheet), drawn with north up (rotation about +19 degrees, unlike the other sheets). Three parts: part 1 Broadway to 16th Avenue between East 53rd and East 55th Streets; part 2 Martha and Kipp Avenues from River Drive to Beech Street; part 3 Martha and Kipp Avenues from block 131 (Bank Street) to Cole Street. Parts 2 and 3 lie along the Garfield borough line.
